# Judges Chapter 20 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_page_289.jpg, JDG_page_290.jpg, JDG_page_291.jpg

1. And all the sons of Yisrael went out, and the congregation assembled as one man, from Dan to Be'er-Sheva and the land of Gil'ad, to YHWH at Mitspah.

2. And the chiefs of all the people, all the tribes of Yisrael, presented themselves in the assembly of the people of God — four hundred thousand men on foot, drawing [the] sword.

3. And the sons of Binyamin heard that the sons of Yisrael had gone up to Mitspah. And the sons of Yisrael said, "Speak — how did this evil come about?"

4. And the Levite man, the husband of the murdered woman, answered and said, "To Giv'ah, which [belongs] to Binyamin, I came — I and my concubine — to spend the night.

5. "And the masters of Giv'ah rose against me and surrounded the house upon me at night. Me they intended to kill, and my concubine they humbled, and she died.

6. "And I seized my concubine and cut her [in pieces] and sent her throughout all the territory of the inheritance of Yisrael, for they have done lewdness and disgraceful folly in Yisrael.

7. "Behold, all of you [are] sons of Yisrael. Give your word and counsel here."

8. And all the people arose as one man, saying, "Not one of us shall go to his tent, and not one of us shall turn aside to his house.

9. "And now, this [is] the thing that we will do to Giv'ah: [We will go up] against it by lot.

10. "And we will take ten men per hundred of all the tribes of Yisrael, and a hundred per thousand, and a thousand per ten thousand, to bring provisions for the people, to do — when they come to Giv'ah of Binyamin — according to all the disgraceful folly that they have done in Yisrael."

11. And every man of Yisrael was gathered against the city, united as one man.

12. And the tribes of Yisrael sent men through all the tribe of Binyamin, saying, "What [is] this evil that has been done among you?

13. "And now, give up the men — the sons of B'liyya'al — who [are] in Giv'ah, and let us put them to death and burn away the evil from Yisrael." And Binyamin was not willing to listen to the voice of their brothers, the sons of Yisrael.

14. And the sons of Binyamin gathered from the cities to Giv'ah, to go out to battle against the sons of Yisrael.

15. And the sons of Binyamin were mustered from the cities on that day — twenty-six thousand men drawing [the] sword, besides the inhabitants of Giv'ah, who were mustered — seven hundred chosen men.

16. Out of all this people, seven hundred chosen men [were] left-handed. Each of these could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.

17. And the men of Yisrael, apart from Binyamin, were mustered — four hundred thousand men drawing [the] sword. All these [were] men of war.

18. And they arose and went up to Beit-El and inquired of God. And the sons of Yisrael said, "Who shall go up first for us to battle against the sons of Binyamin?" And YHWH said, "Y'hudah first."

19. And the sons of Yisrael arose in the morning and encamped against Giv'ah.

20. And the men of Yisrael went out to battle against Binyamin, and the men of Yisrael set themselves in array against them for battle at Giv'ah.

21. And the sons of Binyamin came out from Giv'ah, and they destroyed in Yisrael on that day twenty-two thousand men to the ground.

22. And the people, the men of Yisrael, strengthened themselves and again set themselves in array for battle in the place where they had set themselves in array on the first day.

23. And the sons of Yisrael went up and wept before YHWH until the evening. And they inquired of YHWH, saying, "Shall I again draw near to battle against the sons of Binyamin my brother?" And YHWH said, "Go up against him."

24. And the sons of Yisrael drew near against the sons of Binyamin on the second day.

25. And Binyamin went out against them from Giv'ah on the second day, and they destroyed among the sons of Yisrael again eighteen thousand men to the ground — all these drawing [the] sword.

26. And all the sons of Yisrael and all the people went up and came to Beit-El and wept and sat there before YHWH and fasted on that day until the evening. And they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before YHWH.

27. And the sons of Yisrael inquired of YHWH — and the ark of the covenant of God [was] there in those days,

28. and Pinchas son of El'azar son of Aharon was standing before it in those days — saying, "Shall I go out again to battle against the sons of Binyamin my brother, or shall I cease?" And YHWH said, "Go up, for tomorrow I will give him into your hand."

29. And Yisrael set men in ambush against Giv'ah all around.

30. And the sons of Yisrael went up against the sons of Binyamin on the third day, and they set themselves in array against Giv'ah as at other times.

31. And the sons of Binyamin went out against the people [and] were drawn away from the city. And they began to strike [and] to kill among the people as at other times, on the highways, one of which goes up to Beit-El and one to Giv'ah, in the field — about thirty men of Yisrael.

32. And the sons of Binyamin said, "They are struck before us as at the first." And the sons of Yisrael said, "Let us flee and draw them away from the city to the highways."

33. And all the men of Yisrael rose from their place and set themselves in array at Ba'al-Tamar, and the ambush of Yisrael burst forth from its place, from the clearing of Geva.

34. And there came against Giv'ah ten thousand chosen men from all Yisrael, and the battle was fierce. And they did not know that the evil was touching them.

35. And YHWH struck Binyamin before Yisrael. And the sons of Yisrael destroyed in Binyamin on that day twenty-five thousand and one hundred men — all these drawing [the] sword.

36. And the sons of Binyamin saw that they were struck. And the men of Yisrael gave ground to Binyamin, for they trusted the ambush that they had set against Giv'ah.

37. And the ambush hurried and rushed against Giv'ah, and the ambush spread out and struck the whole city with the edge of the sword.

38. And the appointed signal between the men of Yisrael and the ambush was that they would send up a great column of smoke from the city.

39. And the men of Yisrael turned in the battle. And Binyamin had begun to strike [and] to kill among the men of Yisrael — about thirty men — for they said, "Surely they are utterly struck before us, as [in] the first battle."

40. And the signal began to go up from the city — a column of smoke. And Binyamin looked behind, and behold, the whole of the city went up [in smoke] toward the heavens.

41. And the men of Yisrael turned, and the men of Binyamin were terrified, for they saw that the evil had touched them.

42. And they turned before the men of Yisrael toward the way of the wilderness, and the battle overtook them. And those from the cities were destroying them in their midst.

43. They surrounded Binyamin; they pursued him; they trod him down at [his] resting place as far as opposite Giv'ah toward the sunrise.

44. And there fell of Binyamin eighteen thousand men — all these men of valor.

45. And they turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon. And they gleaned of them on the highways five thousand men. And they pursued hard after them as far as Gid'om and struck of them two thousand men.

46. And all who fell of Binyamin on that day were twenty-five thousand men drawing [the] sword — all these men of valor.

47. And six hundred men turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon and dwelt at the rock of Rimmon four months.

48. And the men of Yisrael turned back against the sons of Binyamin and struck them with the edge of the sword — from the city, men to beast to all that was found. Also all the cities that were found they set on fire.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **v.1 — "from Dan to Be'er-Sheva":** The conventional phrase for all Israel, from the northernmost to southernmost settlement. Ironically, "Dan" here is the newly renamed city from chapter 18 — the product of the theft just narrated.

2. **v.16 — "seven hundred chosen men, left-handed" (itter yad y'mino):** Literally "restricted of his right hand" — the same phrase used of Ehud in 3:15. The Benjaminite left-handed slingers form a devastating force. Binyamin means "son of the right hand," making the left-handed warriors a tribal irony.

3. **v.18 — "Who shall go up first?":** The same question asked in 1:1 — the book's opening. There, Judah went up first against the Canaanites. Here, Judah goes up first against a brother tribe. The echo marks the book's tragic inversion: Israel's war has turned inward.

4. **v.27-28 — Pinchas son of El'azar son of Aharon:** This genealogical detail places the events within two generations of Aaron — far earlier than the narrative's editorial frame in the late Judges period. The note anchors the story to a time when the Aaronic priesthood still functioned at Bethel with the ark.

5. **v.48 — "from the city, men to beast" (m'ir m'tom ad-b'hemah):** The language of cherem (total destruction) — the same language applied to Canaanite cities. Israel applies holy-war destruction to its own brother tribe.

— EMET, AI Translator
